4.odr_com: And his brethren seing that he was loued of his father, more then al his sonnes, they hated him, neither could they speake any thing to him peaceably.

5.s_dismas: It chanced alſo that he reported to his brethren a dreame, that he had ſeene: which occaſion was the ſeed of greater hatred.
5.odr_com: It chanced also that he reported to his brethren a dreame, that he had seene: which occasion was the seed of greater hatred.
5.sabates_a: It chanced also that he reported to his brethren a dream that he had seen, which occasion was the seed of great hatred.

6.sabates_a: And he said to them: hear my dream which I have seen:
6.madueke_b: And he said to them: hear my dream which I have seen:

7.s_dismas: I thought we bounde ſheaues in the field: and my ſheafe aroſe as it were, and ſtood, and your ſheaues ſtanding about did adore my ſheafe.
7.odr_com: I thought we bounde sheaues in the field: and my sheafe arose as it were, and stood, and your sheaues standing about did adore my sheafe.

7.madueke_b: I thought we bound sheaves in the field: and my sheaf arose as it were, and stood, and your sheaves standing about did adore my sheaf.

8.s_dismas: His brethren anſwered: What ſhalt thou be our king? or ſhal we be ſubiect to thy dominion? This occaſion of his dreames and wordes miniſtred nourishment to the enuie and hatred.
8.odr_com: His brethren answered: What shalt thou be our king? or shal we be subiect to thy dominion? This occasion of his dreames and wordes ministred nourishment to the enuie and hatred.
8.sabates_a: His brethren answered: What? Shalt thou be our king? Or shall we be subject to thy dominion? This occasion of his dreams and words ministered nourishment to the envy and hatred.
8.madueke_b: His brethren answered: What? Shalt thou be our king? Or shall we be subject to thy dominion? This occasion of his dreams and words ministered nourishment to the envy and hatred.

9.s_dismas: He ſawe alſo an other dreame, which telling his brethren, he ſaid: I ſawe in a dreame, as it were the ſunne, and the moone, and eleuen ſtarres adore me.
9.odr_com: He sawe also an other dreame, which telling his brethren, he said: I sawe in a dreame, as it were the sunne, and the moone, and eleuen starres adore me.
9.sabates_a: He saw also another dream, which telling his brethren, he said: I saw in a dream, as it were the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars adore me.
9.madueke_b: He saw also another dream, which telling his brethren, he said: I saw in a dream, as it were the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars adore me.

10.s_dismas: Which when he had reported to his father, and brethren, his father rebuked him, and ſaid: What meaneth this dreame that thou haſt ſeene? why ſhal I and thy mother, and thy brethren adore thee vpon the earth?

11.s_dismas: His brethren therfore enuyed him: but his father conſidered the thing with him ſelfe.
11.odr_com: His brethren therfore enuyed him: but his father considered the thing with him selfe.

14.odr_com: I am readie; he said to him: Goe, and see if al things be wel with thy brethren, and the sheepe: and bring me word againe what they doe. Being sent therfore from the Vale of Hebron, he came to Sichem:
14.sabates_a: I am ready; he said to him: Go, and see if all things be well with thy brethren and the sheep, and bring me word again what they do. Being sent therefore from the Vale of Hebron, he came to Sichem:
14.madueke_b: I am ready; he said to him: Go, and see if all things be well with thy brethren and the sheep, and bring me word again what they do. Being sent therefore from the Vale of Hebron, he came to Sichem:

15.s_dismas: and a man found him there wandering in the field, and asked what he ſought.
15.odr_com: and a man found him there wandring in the field, and asked what he sought.
15.sabates_a: and a man found him there wandering in the field, and asked what he sought.
15.madueke_b: and a man found him there wandering in the field, and asked what he sought.

16.s_dismas: But he anſwered: I ſeeke my brethren, ſhew me where they fede the flockes.
16.odr_com: But he answered: I seeke my brethren, shew me where they fede the flockes.
16.sabates_a: But he answered: I seek my brethren, shew me where they feed the flocks.
16.madueke_b: But he answered: I seek my brethren, shew me where they feed the flocks.

17.s_dismas: And the man ſaid to him: They are departed from this place: for I heard them ſay: Let vs goe into Dothain. Ioſeph therfore went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.
17.odr_com: And the man said to him: They are departed from this place: for I heard them say: Let vs goe into Dothain. Ioseph therfore went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.
17.sabates_a: And the man said to him: They are departed from this place: for I heard them say: Let us go into Dothain. Joseph therefore went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.
17.madueke_b: And the man said to him: They are departed from this place: for I heard them say: Let us go into Dothain. Joseph therefore went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.

18.s_dismas: Who when they had ſeene him a farre of, before he came nighe them, they deuiſed to kil him:
18.odr_com: Who when they had seene him a farre of, before he came nighe them, they deuised to kil him:

18.madueke_b: Who when they had seen him a far off, before he came nigh them, they devised to kill him:

19.madueke_b: and spake among themselves: Behold the dreamer cometh,

20.s_dismas: come, let vs kil him, and caſt him into an old ceſterne: and we wil ſay: A naughtie wild beaſt hath deuoured him: and then it ſhal appeare what his dreames doe profite him.
20.odr_com: come, let vs kil him, and cast him into an old cesterne: and we wil say A naughtie wild beast hath deuoured him: and then it shal appeare what his dreames doe profite him.
20.sabates_a: come, let us kill him, and cast him into an old cistern: and we will say a naughty wild beast hath devoured him: and then it shall appear what his dreams do profit him.
20.madueke_b: come, let us kill him, and cast him into an old cistern: and we will say a naughty wild beast hath devoured him: and then it shall appear what his dreams do profit him.

21.s_dismas: And Ruben hearing this, endeuored to deliuer him out of their hands, and ſaid:
21.odr_com: And Ruben hearing this, endeuored to deliuer him out of their hands, and said:
21.sabates_a: And Ruben hearing this, endeavoured to deliver him out of their hands, and said:
21.madueke_b: And Ruben hearing this, endeavoured to deliver him out of their hands, and said:

22.s_dismas: Do not take away his life, neyther ſheed ye blood: but caſt him into this ceſterne, that is in the wilderneſſe, and keepe your handes harmeles: and he ſaid this, deſirous to deliuer him out of their handes, and to reſtore him to his father.
22.odr_com: Do not take away his life, neyther sheed ye blood: but cast him into this cesterne, that is in the wildernesse, and keepe your handes harmeles: and he said this, desirous to deliuer him out of their handes, and to restore him to his father.
22.sabates_a: Do not take away his life, neither shed ye blood: but cast him into this cistern that is in the wilderness, and keep your hands harmless: and he said this, desirous to deliver him out of their hands, and to restore him to his father.
22.madueke_b: Do not take away his life, neither shed ye blood: but cast him into this cistern that is in the wilderness, and keep your hands harmless: and he said this, desirous to deliver him out of their hands, and to restore him to his father.

23.s_dismas: As ſoone therfore as he came vnto his brethren, forthwith they ſtripped him out of his ſide coate, and of diuers colours.
23.odr_com: As soone therfore as he came vnto his brethren, forthwith they stripped him out of his side coate, and of diuers colours.
23.sabates_a: As soon therefore as he came unto his brethren, forthwith they stripped him out of his side coat, and of diverse colours,
23.madueke_b: As soon therefore as he came unto his brethren, forthwith they stripped him out of his side coat, and of diverse colours,

24.s_dismas: And caſt him into the old ceſterne, that had not water.
24.odr_com: And cast him into the old cesterne, that had not water.
24.sabates_a: and cast him into the old cistern, that had not water.
24.madueke_b: and cast him into the old cistern, that had not water.

25.s_dismas: And ſitting to eate bread, they ſaw Iſmaelites wayfaring men cõming from Galaad, and their camels carying ſpices, and roſen, and mirrh into Ægypt.
25.odr_com: And sitting to eate bread, they saw Ismaelites wayfaring men comming from Galaad, and their camels carying spices, and rosen, and mirrh into Ægypt.
25.sabates_a: And sitting to eat bread, they saw Ismaelites wayfaring men coming from Galaad, and their camels carrying spices, and rosen, and myrrh into Ægypt.
25.madueke_b: And sitting to eat bread, they saw Ismaelites wayfaring men coming from Galaad, and their camels carrying spices, and rosen, and myrrh into Aegypt.

26.s_dismas: Iudas therfore ſaid to his brethren: What auaileth it vs if we kil our brother, and conceale his bloode?
26.odr_com: Iudas therfore said to his brethren: What auaileth it vs if we kil our brother, and conceale his bloode?
26.sabates_a: Judas therefore said to his brethren: What availeth it us if we kill our brother, and conceal his blood?
26.madueke_b: Judas therefore said to his brethren: What availeth it us if we kill our brother, and conceal his blood?

27.s_dismas: It is better that he be ſold to the Iſmaelites, and that our handes be not polluted: for he is our brother and our fleſh. His brethren aſſented to his wordes.
27.odr_com: It is better that he be sold to the Ismaelites, and that our handes be not polluted: for he is our brother and our flesh. His brethren assented to his wordes.
27.sabates_a: It is better that he be sold to the Ismaelites, and that our hands be not polluted: for he is our brother and our flesh. His brethren assented to his words.
27.madueke_b: It is better that he be sold to the Ismaelites, and that our hands be not polluted: for he is our brother and our flesh. His brethren assented to his words.

28.s_dismas: And when the Madianite marchants paſſed by, they drawing him out of the ceſterne, ſold him to the Iſmaelites, for twentie peeces of ſiluer, who brought him into Ægypt.
28.odr_com: And when the Madianite marchants passed by, they drawing him out of the cesterne, sold him to the Ismaelites, for twentie peeces of siluer, who brought him into Ægypt.
28.sabates_a: And when the Madianite merchants passed by, they drawing him out of the cistern, sold him to the Ismaelites, for twenty pieces of silver, who brought him into Ægypt.
28.madueke_b: And when the Madianite merchants passed by, they drawing him out of the cistern, sold him to the Ismaelites, for twenty pieces of silver, who brought him into Aegypt.

29.s_dismas: And Ruben returning to the ceſterne, findeth not the boy:
29.odr_com: And Ruben returning to the cesterne, findeth not the boy:
29.sabates_a: And Ruben returning to the cistern, findeth not the boy:
29.madueke_b: And Ruben returning to the cistern, findeth not the boy:

30.s_dismas: and renting his garments went to his brethren, and ſaid: The boy doth not appeare, and whither shal I goe?
30.odr_com: and renting his garments went to his brethren, and said: The boy doth not appeare, and whither shal I goe?
30.sabates_a: and renting his garments went to his brethren, and said: The boy doth not appear, and whither shall I go?
30.madueke_b: and renting his garments went to his brethren, and said: The boy doth not appear, and whither shall I go?

31.s_dismas: And they tooke his coate, and dipped it in the blood of a kidde, which they had killed:
31.odr_com: And they tooke his coate, and dipped it in the blood of a kidde, which they had killed:
31.sabates_a: And they took his coat, and dipped it in the blood of a kid which they had killed,
31.madueke_b: And they took his coat, and dipped it in the blood of a kid which they had killed,

32.s_dismas: ſending ſome that should carie it to their father, and should ſay: This we haue founde: ſee whether it be thy ſonnes coate, or no.
32.odr_com: sending some that should carie it to their father, and should say: This we haue founde: see whether it be thy sonnes coate, or no.
32.sabates_a: sending some that should carry it to their father, and should say: This we have found: see whether it be thy son's coat, or no.
32.madueke_b: sending some that should carry it to their father, and should say: This we have found: see whether it be thy son's coat, or no.

33.s_dismas: Which when the father acknowledged, he ſaid: It is my ſonnes coate, a naughtie wild beaſt hath eaten him, a beaſt hath deuoured Ioſeph.
33.odr_com: Which when the father acknowledged, he said: It is my sonnes coate, a naughtie wild beast hath eaten him, a beast hath deuoured Ioseph.
33.sabates_a: Which when the father acknowledged, he said: It is my son's coat, a naughty wild beast hath eaten him, a beast hath devoured Joseph.
33.madueke_b: Which when the father acknowledged, he said: It is my son's coat, a naughty wild beast hath eaten him, a beast hath devoured Joseph.

34.s_dismas: And tearing his garments, did on ſackcloth, mourning his ſonne a great time.
34.odr_com: And tearing his garments, did on sackcloth, mourning his sonne a great time.
34.sabates_a: And tearing his garments, did on sackcloth, mourning his son a great time.
34.madueke_b: And tearing his garments, did on sackcloth, mourning his son a great time.

35.s_dismas: And al his children being gethered together to aſſwage their fathers ſorowe, he would not take comforte, but ſaid: I wil deſcend vnto my ſonne into hel, mourning. And whileſt he perſeuered in weeping,
35.odr_com: And al his children being gethered together to asswage their fathers sorowe, he would not take comforte, but said: I wil descend vnto my sonne into hel, mourning. And whilest he perseuered in weeping,
35.sabates_a: And all his children being gathered together to assuage their father's sorrow, he would not take comfort, but said: I will descend unto my son into hell, mourning. And whilst he persevered in weeping,
35.madueke_b: And all his children being gathered together to assuage their father's sorrow, he would not take comfort, but said: I will descend unto my son into hell, mourning. And whilst he persevered in weeping,

36.odr_com: the Madianites sold Ioseph in Ægypt to Phutiphar an Eunuch of Pharoes maister of the souldiars.

36.madueke_b: the Madianites sold Joseph in Aegypt to Putiphar an Eunuch of Pharao's, master of the soldiers.

janvier_by_verse.1: And Jacob dwelt in the land of Chanaan, wherein his father sojourned.
janvier_by_verse.2: And these are his generations: Joseph when he was sixteen years old, fed the flock with his brethren being yet a boy: and he was with the sons of Bala and Zelpha his father's wives: and he accused his brethren to his father of a most wicked crime.
janvier_by_verse.3: And Israel loved Joseph above all his sons, because he had begotten him in his old age and he made him a coat of diverse colours.
janvier_by_verse.4: And his brethren seeing that he was loved of his father more than all his sons, they hated him, neither could they speak any thing to him peaceably.
janvier_by_verse.5: It chanced also that he reported to his brethren a dream that he had seen, which occasion was the seed of great hatred.
janvier_by_verse.6: And he said to them: hear my dream which I have seen:
janvier_by_verse.7: I thought we bound sheaves in the field: and my sheaf arose as it were, and stood, and your sheaves standing about did adore my sheaf.
janvier_by_verse.8: His brethren answered: What? Shalt thou be our king? Or shall we be subject to thy dominion? This occasion of his dreams and words ministered nourishment to the envy and hatred.
janvier_by_verse.9: He saw also another dream, which telling his brethren, he said: I saw in a dream, as it were the sun, and the moon, and eleven stars adore me.
janvier_by_verse.10: Which when he had reported to his father and brethren, his father rebuked him, and said: What meaneth this dream that thou hast seen? Why, shall I and thy mother, and thy brethren adore thee upon the earth?
janvier_by_verse.11: His brethren therefore envied him: but his father considered the thing with himself.
janvier_by_verse.12: And when his brethren abode in Sichem feeding their father's flocks,
janvier_by_verse.13: Israel said to him: Thy brethren feed sheep in Sichem: come, I will send thee to them. Who answering,
janvier_by_verse.14: I am ready; he said to him: Go, and see if all things be well with thy brethren and the sheep, and bring me word again what they do. Being sent therefore from the Vale of Hebron, he came to Sichem:
janvier_by_verse.15: and a man found him there wandering in the field, and asked what he sought.
janvier_by_verse.16: But he answered: I seek my brethren, shew me where they feed the flocks.
janvier_by_verse.17: And the man said to him: They are departed from this place: for I heard them say: Let us go into Dothain. Joseph therefore went forward after his brethren, and found them in Dothain.
janvier_by_verse.18: Who when they had seen him a far off, before he came nigh them, they devised to kill him:
